title: FDM production derating rules on a peak stress: static / creep-table / fatigue / temperature / anisotropy

governing_equations.name: static rule
governing_equations.expr: SF_static = (yield_mpa * derate) / demand_mpa ;  pass iff SF_static >= safety_factor_required
governing_equations.description: demand_mpa = max_von_mises_pa / 1e6 from a prior ace_fea; yield_mpa is the material's tools/material_db.json cell; derate = layer_adhesion_factor when the anisotropy rule fires, else 1.

governing_equations.name: creep rule (sustained load)
governing_equations.expr: allow_creep = creep.sig_allow_mpa[T_row][t_col] * (z_vs_xy_strength_ratio if across_layer else 1) ;  SF_creep = allow_creep / demand_mpa
governing_equations.description: Read through tools/materials.py creep_lookup — the ONE reader of the material record's temperature x duration table. DEFAULT: both axes round UP to the next tabulated cell (a conservative step: an in-between request reads the worse cell). OPT-IN (job key creep_interpolation:true): the allowable is interpolated between the bracketing cells instead — a(T,t) = a_lo(t) + (T-T_lo)/(T_hi-T_lo) * (a_hi(t)-a_lo(t)), with a_row(t) log-linear in t between its two columns — and the row says basis 'interpolated', names both cells, and carries the bucket the default would have read. Above the hottest tabulated tier, without a duration_h, or for a material with no table the row REFUSES either way (allowable 0.0, pass false, refusal_kind named) — the legacy yield x creep_sustained_fraction scalar is reported as legacy_scalar_mpa and is never the allowable.

governing_equations.name: fatigue rule (cyclic load)
governing_equations.expr: allow_fatigue = ultimate_mpa * fatigue_knockdown * derate ;  SF_fatigue = allow_fatigue / demand_mpa
governing_equations.description: ~1e6-cycle allowable as a knockdown fraction of ultimate (engineering rule of thumb, NOT a measured S-N curve — ace_fatigue is the S-N tool).

governing_equations.name: temperature rule
governing_equations.expr: pass iff service_temp_c <= service_temp_c_limit ;  SF_temp = limit / service (reported, no factor applied)
governing_equations.description: The HDT-class limit IS the derated number; no safety factor is applied to temperature.

governing_equations.name: anisotropy rule (scalar-tier)
governing_equations.expr: theta = asin(|load . build| / (|load| |build|)) ;  if theta > 30 deg: derate = layer_adhesion_factor and an explicit across-layer static row is added
governing_equations.description: Load-DIRECTION heuristic only (across-layer strength / in-plane strength); not a layer-normal stress-tensor check. Skipped WITH a note when orientation is absent — never silently.

assumptions: The demand is a single scalar peak von Mises stress from a prior analysis; the tool does no geometry or FEA and inherits the upstream error band (voxel ace_fea under-reads coarse peaks ~20%).
Allowables are TYPICAL desktop-FDM datasheet-class values in tools/material_db.json (as-printed XY), to be verified per filament brand.
The creep table (tools/materials/pla.json#creep.sig_allow_mpa) is a conservative CONSTRUCTION from published printed-PLA creep/rupture data, not a measured design curve; only PLA carries one.

Opt-in creep interpolation assumes the allowable varies linearly with temperature between the two tabulated rows and log-linearly with duration between two tabulated columns; the bracketing cells are the only data and no measured cell is invented.
Fatigue knockdown and creep fraction are rules of thumb, not measured filament data; the anisotropy rule is scalar-tier.
Overall verdict ok = every evaluated rule passes; skipped rules are listed with a reason.

boundary_conditions.fixtures: not applicable — the 'boundary' is the service condition: service_temp_c (default 25), duration_h (REQUIRED when sustained — never defaulted), load_character {sustained, cyclic}, orientation {build_dir, primary_load_dir}, creep_interpolation (default false).
boundary_conditions.loads: max_von_mises_pa (Pa) — the peak stress being graded.
boundary_conditions.selector_count_unit: rules evaluated (each rule = one receipt row)

discretization.element: none — rule arithmetic over table cells; the creep table is a step (rounded up on both axes) or, opt-in, a bilinear (T-linear x ln t-linear) interpolation between bracketing cells
discretization.notes: No iteration. Deterministic: no clock, no RNG; the receipt is byte-identical across runs; receipts that never asked for interpolation are byte-identical to those before the option existed.

additional_pins: tools/production_check.py --selftest (the pinned PETG gate + the PLA creep-table contract + the interpolation opt-in)
tools/materials_crosslang_test.py (540-probe Python/Rust creep-cell pin of the DEFAULT reader)
validation.ground_truth: Hand-derived from the material tables, arithmetic stated in the pin: PLA static SF = 55/10 = 5.5; PLA creep 23 C / 1 y = table cell 2.5 MPa (SF 2.5 at 1 MPa), 23 C / 24 h = 5.0 MPa, 25 C rounds UP to the 55 C row (0.5 MPa at 30 d); across-layer 55 x 0.55 = 30.25 MPa static and 2.5 x 0.55 = 1.375 MPa creep; fatigue 60 x 0.3 = 18 MPa; temperature 60 C > 55 C fails with SF 55/60; refusals: sustained without duration_h -> refusal.creep_duration_required, 70 C sustained -> refusal.creep_temp_above_tabulated, PETG sustained -> refusal.creep_no_table (each ok:false, allowable 0.0, exit 2); an unknown material exits 1; opt-in interpolation at 30 C / 24 h = 5.0 + (30-23)/(55-23) x (1.5-5.0) = 4.234375 MPa with basis 'interpolated' and both cells named while the default still reads 1.5 MPa, 23 C / 12 h = 7.5 + ln12/ln24 x (5.0-7.5) = 5.545261 MPa (log-linear), and the flag still refuses at 70 C.

error_band.rule_arithmetic: exact to 1e-9 MPa (receipt rounds to 4 decimals; the pin compares at 1e-4) — measured 0.0
error_band.refusal_contract: exact: refusal rows carry allowable 0.0, pass false, the named refusal_kind, and exit 2 — measured as specified
error_band.interpolation: exact to the receipt's 4-decimal rounding against the hand formula — measured 2.5e-5 (rounding only)
error_band.determinism: stdout receipt byte-identical across reruns — measured identical

validation.direction: no bias in the arithmetic; the DEFAULT creep lookup (round up on both axes) is deliberately conservative — it reads the worse cell; interpolation is opt-in, labelled, and always lies between the two bracketing cells (monotone table).

caveats: This is a RULES engine over datasheet-class tables, not a physics simulation: the verdict is only as good as the table cells and the upstream stress.

The default creep lookup is a STEP: a 25 C declared ambient reads the 55 C row (7x lower than the 23 C row) — declare 23 C, accept the 55 C row, or opt in to creep_interpolation:true and quote basis 'interpolated' with both cells.

Interpolated creep allowables are a model between two conservative constructions, not measurements; the 55 C long-duration cells are BOUNDS, so anything interpolated toward them inherits that status (the LOWEST bracketing confidence governs); interpolation has no Rust mirror.
Anisotropy is scalar-tier (load direction only); a tensor layer-normal check needs an ACE solver change.
The demand inherits ace_fea's ~20% coarse-mesh under-prediction of peak bending stress — margin accordingly.
Only PLA has a creep table; every other material REFUSES a sustained-load verdict outright.

limits_of_validity.regime: as-printed FDM thermoplastics in tools/material_db.json (PLA|PETG|ABS|ASA|TPU95A|PC|PA); scalar peak-stress grading
limits_of_validity.resolution: creep: PLA 23 C and 55 C rows x 1 h / 24 h / 30 d / 1 y columns; nothing above 55 C (refused, with or without interpolation); between rows/columns the default rounds up and the opt-in interpolates (never extrapolates)
